name: Pet Vaccination Checklist
description: A checklist to help pet owners understand core vaccines, track records, and stay on schedule with their veterinarian's guidance.

items.text: Confirm your pet's age, weight, and health status
Gather any prior vaccination records you have
Ask your vet which vaccines are due now
Note any past reactions to vaccines or medicines
Schedule the visit and plan any needed boosters
items.note: Ask your vet to confirm the right plan for your pet

items.text: Rabies vaccine, often required by law
Distemper protection for your pet's species
Parvovirus for dogs as part of core care
Adenovirus and parainfluenza for dogs as advised
Feline panleukopenia and respiratory viruses for cats
items.note: Core recommendations vary by region and vet, so confirm with your vet

items.text: Bordetella for dogs that board or socialize
Leptospirosis based on local risk and exposure
Canine influenza for higher-contact dogs
Lyme disease where ticks are common
Feline leukemia for cats with outdoor access
Vaccine name and what it protects against
Date given and the clinic or vet who administered it
Lot or batch number when provided
Next due date for the booster
Any reaction noted in the hours after the shot
Watch for mild soreness, tiredness, or low appetite
Note any swelling, vomiting, or distress to report
Give your pet a calm space to rest
Update your records and set the next reminder
Keep a copy ready for boarding or travel
items.note: Contact your vet promptly if you see a strong or lasting reaction

items.text: Set calendar reminders for upcoming boosters
Review the plan at each wellness visit
Update records when you change vets or move
Keep a digital backup of the vaccination history
Ask about combining due vaccines into one visit
This checklist is general information for owners, not veterinary advice; vaccine schedules vary by region and vet and by your pet's needs, so always consult a licensed veterinarian
items.note: For any reaction or emergency, contact your vet or an emergency animal hospital immediately

faq.q: What is the difference between core and non-core vaccines?
faq.a: Core vaccines are recommended for most pets because they protect against serious, widespread diseases. Non-core, or lifestyle, vaccines are given based on risk factors like travel or contact with other animals. Your vet decides which apply.

faq.q: How do I know which vaccines my pet needs?
faq.a: Your veterinarian recommends vaccines based on your pet's species, age, lifestyle, and where you live. Bring your pet's history to each visit so the plan can be updated as needed.

faq.q: How often do pets need booster shots?
faq.a: Boosters keep protection up to date, but intervals vary by vaccine, age, and local guidelines. Some are given yearly and others less often. Follow the schedule your veterinarian sets for your pet.

faq.q: Why should I keep vaccination records?
faq.a: Records prove your pet is protected and are often required for boarding, grooming, daycare, and travel. They also help any vet quickly see what is current and what is due.

faq.q: Is this pet vaccination checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, record each vaccine and date, and bring it to appointments to keep your pet's schedule on track.
